context_observations: Fictional synthetic schematic case. Prototype last confirmed 18:00 and missing 18:18. Shift assignments: Nora teal, Eli orange, Maya purple, Theo blue, Ada red. Coat colour is not biometric identity.

exhibits.title: Floor plan
exhibits.direct_observation: The schematic connects the lab through the east corridor to the east exit. A second link joins the lab and service corridor, labelled UNMONITORED LINK TO LAB. A cafeteria is drawn separately.
exhibits.interpretation: Both the east route and service link provide possible approaches to the lab.
exhibits.uncertainty: No scale, travel times, door permissions, or complete loading-bay/reception connections are given. The drawing does not establish that anyone used either route.

exhibits.title: Prototype last visible
exhibits.direct_observation: The LAB frame labelled CAMERA 18:00 shows a gray rectangular case/object with a black triangular marking on the brown bench.
exhibits.interpretation: With the case brief and V09, this is the prototype reference appearance and last confirmed presence.
exhibits.uncertainty: The schematic shows exterior appearance, not a serial number or contents.

exhibits.title: East corridor
exhibits.direct_observation: The EAST CORRIDOR frame labelled CAMERA 18:10 shows one teal-coated figure, with no carried object drawn.
exhibits.interpretation: Appearance is consistent with Nora’s assigned coat; D01 records Nora’s credential entering this corridor at the same minute.
exhibits.uncertainty: Coat and badge correspondence is not biometric identification. One still does not show the figure’s subsequent route or hidden possessions.

exhibits.title: Two service-door figures
exhibits.direct_observation: The SERVICE DOOR frame labelled CAMERA 18:14 shows two gray-coated figures. No prototype, triangle-marked case, or other carried object is drawn.
exhibits.interpretation: The frame is compatible with two people near the service door when credentials for both Eli and Maya were recorded there.
exhibits.uncertainty: Gray appearances cannot distinguish the assigned orange and purple coats or identify either figure. The still does not establish entry direction, lab entry, possession, removal, or collaboration.

exhibits.title: Prototype missing
exhibits.direct_observation: The LAB frame labelled CAMERA 18:18 shows the bench without the gray triangle-marked object seen in V02.
exhibits.interpretation: The prototype is absent from its shown location by 18:18, consistent with the brief.
exhibits.uncertainty: The image does not show the removal or exclude relocation elsewhere in the lab.

exhibits.title: Cafeteria
exhibits.direct_observation: The CAFETERIA frame labelled CAMERA 18:12 shows one blue-coated figure and no carried object drawn.
exhibits.interpretation: Consistent with Theo’s assigned coat and the cafeteria entry under Theo’s credential in D01.
exhibits.uncertainty: It corroborates one moment, not Theo’s claim of remaining there continuously.

exhibits.title: Reception
exhibits.direct_observation: The RECEPTION frame labelled CAMERA 18:13 shows one red-coated figure and no carried object drawn.
exhibits.interpretation: Consistent with Ada’s assigned coat and the reception entry under Ada’s credential in D01.
exhibits.uncertainty: A still and entry record cannot establish Ada’s location throughout the 18-minute window.

exhibits.title: Loading bay box
exhibits.direct_observation: The LOADING BAY frame labelled CAMERA 18:11 shows one purple-coated figure beside a plain brown rectangular box. No triangle marking is drawn on the box.
exhibits.interpretation: Consistent with Maya carrying a cardboard supply box as stated in D02 and with the consumables-box request in D03. The visible object differs from V02/V09.
exhibits.uncertainty: Material and contents cannot be established from a schematic; the box could conceal something, but no supplied evidence shows that it does. Coat colour does not prove identity.

exhibits.title: Object reference
exhibits.direct_observation: The OBJECT DETAIL / CAMERA REFERENCE image shows a gray rectangular case/object with a black triangle on the bench; no event time is given.
exhibits.interpretation: The distinctive exterior supports comparing the prototype in V02 with a visually matching object elsewhere.
exhibits.uncertainty: A matching exterior is not unique identification or proof of contents.

exhibits.title: Service-camera coverage notice
exhibits.direct_observation: The SERVICE CAMERA / CAMERA MAINTENANCE exhibit reads BLIND SPOT: SERVICE CORRIDOR.
exhibits.interpretation: Together with V01 and D03 this leaves a possible service approach unobserved.
exhibits.uncertainty: It does not prove use of the route. A view of the service door, if supplied, would not eliminate the corridor blind spot.

exhibits.title: Access records
exhibits.direct_observation: Five rows: 18:10 Nora Vale / EAST_CORRIDOR / ENTRY; 18:12 Theo Park / CAFETERIA / ENTRY; 18:13 Ada Finch / RECEPTION / ENTRY; 18:14 Eli Stone / SERVICE_DOOR / ENTRY; 18:14 Maya Reed / SERVICE_DOOR / ENTRY.
exhibits.interpretation: Eli’s and Maya’s credentials both appear at the service door in the same minute as V04’s two figures, giving both an opportunity lead.
exhibits.uncertainty: Minute resolution does not establish precise order or simultaneity. Credentials do not identify the gray figures or prove that either person entered the lab or removed the prototype.

exhibits.title: Witness statements
exhibits.direct_observation: Five explicitly unverified statements: Nora says she only visited the east corridor and left; Eli says he did not approach the lab after 18:00; Maya says she carried a cardboard supply box at 18:11; Theo says he remained in the cafeteria from 18:12; Ada says she staffed reception.
exhibits.interpretation: Statements supply claims to test against the images and access records, rather than established alibis.
exhibits.uncertainty: No interview times, independent identity authentication, full movement accounts, or corroboration of continuous presence are supplied.

exhibits.title: Internal messages
exhibits.direct_observation: 17:00 Eli says his project needs the prototype tomorrow. 17:10 Maya requests moving the cardboard consumables box to the loading bay. 17:20 Security says coat descriptions come from shift assignments and doors log badge credentials, not biometric identity. Service corridor is a camera blind spot.
exhibits.interpretation: Eli’s message establishes a stated need, not theft. Maya’s request supports a routine-box explanation. Security limits identity attribution and clarifies coverage or timing.
exhibits.uncertainty: Messages do not prove intent, compliance with the box request, custody of badges/coats, or the actual removal sequence.
